title: Runway Excursion Incident Involving Cessna C172 trainer Aircraft at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra
body_text:
A runway excursion incident involving a Cessna C172 type aircraft, registration VT-SEX, operated by Academy of Carver Aviation, a DGCA approved Flying Training Organization occurred at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra, on 09 August 2026 at approximately 12:25 PM.
The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise. The aircraft was under the command of Capt. Chirag Shashikant Doifode, Flight Instructor with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.
The aircraft taxied out at approximately 0639 UTC (1209 IST) for the scheduled training exercise. During the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of Runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out. Subsequently, the aircraft lined up at the threshold of Runway 11 and another rejected take-off exercise was carried out.
During the course of the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of Runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion.
There were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities.
The DGCA Air Safety team is proceeding to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident. Further information will be shared as and when it is verified and becomes available.
***
Divyanshu Kumar

enrichment.summary: A Cessna C172 trainer aircraft (VT-SEX), operated by Academy of Carver Aviation, suffered a runway excursion at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra, on 9 August 2026 during a Circuit and Landing Emergencies training exercise. While practising a rejected take-off, the aircraft failed to stop within the paved runway and veered off beyond the threshold of Runway 29. No injuries or fatalities occurred, though the aircraft sustained damage to its propeller, engine cowling, and nose landing gear. DGCA's Air Safety team is conducting a preliminary investigation.
enrichment.context: Flying Training Organizations (FTOs) approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) conduct mandatory training exercises like rejected take-offs and circuit emergencies to prepare trainee pilots for real-world contingencies. Runway excursions—where an aircraft departs the runway surface during takeoff or landing—are among the most common categories of aviation incidents worldwide, often linked to factors such as runway condition, aircraft speed, pilot judgment, or mechanical issues. India's civil aviation safety architecture relies on DGCA for licensing, regulation, and incident investigation, while more serious accidents may involve the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB). This incident, involving a training aircraft with no casualties, underscores the routine safety oversight mechanisms in India's civil aviation sector, particularly concerning flying schools that train future commercial pilots amid rising demand for pilots in India's expanding aviation market.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following bodies is primarily responsible for aviation safety regulation and investigating incidents involving Flying Training Organizations in India?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
prelims_questions.explanation: The DGCA is India's primary regulatory body for civil aviation safety, licensing, and oversight of flying training organizations, including conducting preliminary investigations into incidents.

prelims_questions.question: A 'runway excursion' in aviation terminology refers to which of the following?
options: An aircraft taking off from an unauthorized runway
An aircraft veering off or overrunning the paved runway surface
A scheduled diversion of an aircraft to another airport
An unauthorized entry of a vehicle onto an active runway
prelims_questions.explanation: A runway excursion occurs when an aircraft departs the paved runway surface, either by veering off the side or overrunning the end, as happened in this incident at Baramati Airfield.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the regulatory framework governing civil aviation safety in India, with special reference to the role of DGCA in overseeing Flying Training Organizations.
Examine the challenges facing India's pilot training ecosystem and suggest measures to strengthen safety protocols in flying training organizations.
